entities.summary:
Saint Begga was the daughter of Pepin of Landen, mayor of the palace of Austrasia, and his wife Itta. She is also the grandmother of Charles Martel, who is the grandfather of Charlemagne. 

Born in the 7th century, Begga's life was marked by her family's significant role in the Merovingian dynasty, which ruled Francia during the early Middle Ages. As a member of the royal family, Begga was well-educated and played a crucial role in the governance of Austrasia, which covered much of modern-day France, Belgium, and parts of Germany and the Netherlands. 

Begga's influence extended beyond her family's political power, as she also played a key role in the spread of Christianity in the region. She was a patron of the church and worked closely with the bishop of Trier, a major center of Christianity in the region. 

Begga's legacy can be seen in the many churches and monasteries she founded, including the famous Abbey of St. Martin in Tours, which became a major center of learning and culture in medieval Europe. The abbey's scriptorium produced many illuminated manuscripts, including the famous Book of Kells, which remains one of the most famous examples of Insular art. 

In conclusion, Saint Begga's life and legacy are a testament to the enduring power of family, faith, and education in shaping the course of human history. She may not have been a world-changing figure, but her influence was significant within the context of medieval Europe and continues to inspire scholars and historians today.
